dictate.title: Dictate anywhere
dictate.summary: Let your voice do the typing.
dictate.body: Place your cursor in a text field, hold {{binding}}, speak naturally, and release. Start here, then try a sentence in an email draft or message. Wait for the text before switching apps. You can change your shortcut in Settings → Dictation.

capture.title: Save a thought or task
capture.summary: Keep an idea without finding somewhere to type.
capture.body: Dictation types at your cursor. Log Capture saves a thought or task to Tucky. Hold {{logBinding}}, say what’s on your mind, then release. Review the suggested type and project before saving. Once saved, it appears in the Dashboard.

retrieve.title: Find it again
retrieve.summary: Bring a saved thought back when you need it.
retrieve.body: Open Dashboard search and enter a word you remember from a capture. Open a result to read it. Your third getting-started step completes when you open a matching capture.

projects.title: Give your work a home
projects.summary: Keep related thoughts in one project.
projects.body: Create a project with a clear name and a short description. Choose it while reviewing a capture, or organize existing captures later. Projects appear in your sidebar.

tasks.title: Turn a thought into a next step
tasks.summary: Review a task, set a deadline, and check it off.
tasks.body: A task captured by voice appears under Tasks in the Dashboard. Open it to adjust its deadline. Check it off when the work is done.

chat.title: Ask your memory a question
chat.summary: Find connections across your saved captures.
chat.body: Open Chat, start a new conversation, and ask “What did I capture today?” Use the source links to check the answer. More useful captures give Chat more to work with.

meetings.title: Leave a meeting with useful notes
meetings.summary: Capture the conversation and revisit the important parts.
meetings.body: Use the meeting Record button when you’re ready, or choose how Tucky offers to record supported calls in Settings. Let participants know you’re recording. System audio permission captures the other voices; the optional smart model creates summaries. You can stop at any time.

people.title: Remember the people behind the meeting
people.summary: Build useful context for your next conversation.
people.body: Confirm meeting speakers and link them to people. People & companies brings their confirmed meeting history together. Choose a person to create a Prep brief before your next conversation.

daily.title: Start the day with yesterday in view
daily.summary: Revisit your meetings, notes, and dictations.
daily.body: Daily recaps bring yesterday’s saved activity together. Open Daily recaps to read or generate one. You can choose morning delivery and weekdays in Settings → Daily Recap.

recordings.title: Show it once
recordings.summary: Capture a screen walkthrough, then edit or share it.
recordings.body: Use Record screen in the sidebar to choose what to capture. After recording, open it from Dashboard → Recordings to edit, export, or generate a transcript. Google Drive sharing is optional; review who can access the upload before sharing.

templates.title: Say it, then shape it
templates.summary: Turn spoken thoughts into an email or a list.
templates.body: Voice format templates rewrite your words before they’re pasted. Review the available templates in Settings, then use the action shortcut or enable the spoken trigger to request a format. Your ordinary dictation shortcut still works as usual.

actions.title: A shortcut for the little things
actions.summary: Use voice commands to open apps and more.
actions.body: Settings → Actions shows your current action shortcut, trigger preferences, and examples. Try a simple app launch first. Review settings before using actions that draft emails or change counters.

export.title: Take your captures with you
export.summary: Keep useful notes beside your other work.
export.body: Dashboard’s Export menu saves activity as Markdown or CSV. For an ongoing workflow, choose an export folder for a project in Settings. Meeting notes can also have their own folder.

agents.title: Give your coding tools useful context
agents.summary: Let a connected agent search the work you’ve captured.
agents.body: Settings → Coding Agents lets you connect a supported tool and choose what it may access. Search access and screen-recording access are separate controls. Start with only the access you need.

startup.title: Make room for one easy habit
startup.summary: Try your first message of the day by voice.
startup.body: Pick a moment you already repeat: your first email, a note after a call, or a thought before closing your laptop. Use Tucky for that one moment. Launch at login can keep your shortcut ready when you start work.
